title: Microfluidics and fluorescence microscopy protocol to study the response of C. elegans to chemosensory stimuli
protocol: Sedate worms.
Select approximately 10 young adult worms from the desired strain.
Place selected worms in a droplet of 10 μL 5 mM levamisole.
Cover the droplet with a small petri dish to prevent evaporation.
Incubate the worms for approximately 15 minutes until fully sedated and motionless.
Insert the steel pin to the inlet of the chip’s worm channel to insert the worm.
Manually apply pressure to insert the worm.
Fill four 3 mL syringes with the appropriate solutions: syringe 1 and 4 with 5 μm fluorescein; syringe 2 with your chemosensory stimulus and syringe 3 with M13 buffer.
Connect the syringes to a pressure controller via Tygon tubing.
Connect the syringes with Tygon tubing and a stainless-steel pin to the fluidic inlets of the microfluidics chip.
Put the sample under the microscope.

Close three of the four fluidic inlets with a closed steel pin, replace the steel pin connected to the M13-filled syringe to the waste outlet, and manually apply pressure on the syringe to let the worm leave the chip via the (open) fourth fluidic inlet.
Suck up a worm, head-first, using a stainless steel pin connected to an M13-filled syringe.
Insert the steel pin into the inlet of the chip’s worm channel.
Apply pressure gently to ensure the worm enters the worm trap tail-first.
Gently continue applying pressure until the worm is at the appropriate position in the trap.
If the worm does not enter smoothly or gets stuck, change the direction of flow back and forth slightly by pushing and pulling on the plunger.
Leave the syringe connected to the insert of the worm trap and close the valve.
Fill four 3 mL syringes with appropriate solutions: syringe 1 and 4 with 5 μm fluorescein; syringe 2 with chemosensory stimulus; syringe 3 with M13 buffer.
Connect the syringes to a pressure controller via Tygon tubing.
Connect the syringes with Tygon tubing and stainless-steel pin to fluidic inlets of microfluidics chip.
Put sample under microscope using a 10× objective.
Apply 100 mbar to channels 1, 3, and 4; apply 90 mbar to channel 2.
Apply 100 mbar to channels 1, 3, and 4.
Apply 90 mbar to channel 2.
Decrease the pressure on channel 2 to 0 mbar.
Wait for approximately 10 seconds.
Put all pressures to 0 mbar.
Wait for approximately 10 seconds.
Apply 100 mbar to channels 1, 3, and 4 again.
Apply 90 mbar to channel 2 again.
Determine appropriate pressures for ‘stimulus OFF’.
Save settings for ‘stimulus OFF’.
Switch to ‘stimulus OFF’ and wait until fluorescein from channel 2 has disappeared.
Remain in ‘stimulus OFF’ mode.
Imaging timing: approximately 10 minutes.
Depend on research question, switch to appropriate objective (40× air or 100× oil).
Bring phasmid chemosensory cilia into focus.
Start acquiring images for baseline measurement.
Switch pressures to ‘stimulus ON’.
Write down frame number when switching stimulus on.
Switch back to ‘stimulus OFF’ mode when you want to stop the stimulus.
Write down the frame number.
Stop acquiring images when you want to end your measurement.
Put all pressures to 0 mbar and disconnect the tubings from the chip.
Use the syringe connected to the worm channel to push the worm out of the trap by applying manual pressure.
Close three fluidic inlets with a closed steel pin.
Replace the steel pin connected to the M13-filled syringe to the waste outlet.
Manually apply pressure on the syringe to let the worm leave the chip via the open 4th fluidic inlet.
Clean the chip by flushing it with milliQ after the last experiment of the day.
Pause point: Worms can be imaged for up to two hours after sedation. Sedate a new batch of worms after this period.
